config.title: Write typed groupBy helper

intro.title: Write typed groupBy helper
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed `groupBy` helper function in TypeScript. This function will take an array of objects and group them by a specified property, returning an object where keys are the property values and values are arrays of matching items. You'll learn to use TypeScript generics and keyof to create flexible, type-safe utility functions. This exercise will help you understand how to write reusable code with strong type checking. By the end, you'll have a practical tool for organizing data in your applications.
intro.usecase: A typed `groupBy` helper is essential for organizing and displaying categorized data in real-world applications. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, you might use it to group products by category (Electronics, Clothing, Books) to render distinct sections or filter panels. In a project management tool, it can group tasks by status (To Do, In Progress, Done) to populate separate Kanban columns. This pattern ensures type safety when transforming API data into structured UI components, preventing runtime errors and improving developer confidence in data handling.

objectives: Implement a basic groupBy function that accepts an array and a key selector
Configure type parameters to define input and output types for the groupBy helper
Apply TypeScript generics to create a reusable typed utility function
Manipulate array data structures to organize items into grouped collections
Construct a return type that maps keys to arrays of corresponding values
Initialize a typed accumulator object to store grouped results
Integrate the key selector callback to extract grouping criteria from array elements

steps.title: Import TypeScript and define the groupBy function signature
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript file and define a function named 'groupBy' with generic type parameters for the array and key, returning a typed object.
steps.hint: Start with 'function groupBy' or 'const groupBy =' and include generic type parameters <T, K> before the parameter list.
steps.seedCode: // Create the groupBy function with generic types
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function signature for groupBy with proper TypeScript generics.
successCriteria: The groupBy function is defined with generic type parameters <T, K> and returns a typed object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named 'groupBy' with generic type parameters <T, K>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature isn't quite right. Define a function named 'groupBy' with generic type parameters <T, K> that will return a typed object.

steps.title: Define the function parameters with proper typing
steps.instruction: Add the two parameters to your groupBy function: an array of type T[] and a keySelector function that takes an item of type T and returns a key of type K (where K extends string | number | symbol).
steps.hint: The function signature should look like: groupBy<T, K extends string | number | symbol>(items: T[], keySelector: (item: T) => K).
steps.expectedOutcome: Your groupBy function will have properly typed parameters ready for implementation.
successCriteria: The groupBy function has two parameters: items (type T[]) and keySelector (type (item: T) => K) with correct generic constraints.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both parameters with the correct types: items should be T[] and keySelector should be (item: T) => K.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parameters aren't properly typed. Check the generic constraints and parameter types.

steps.title: Initialize the result object with proper typing
steps.instruction: Inside the groupBy function, declare a variable named 'result' and initialize it as an empty object with the type Record<K, T[]>.
steps.hint: Use the Record utility type to specify that the object will have keys of type K and values of type arrays of T.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function now has a properly typed accumulator object ready to store grouped results.
successCriteria: A variable 'result' is declared with type Record<K, T[]> and initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure 'result' has the exact type Record<K, T[]> and is initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The result object initialization is missing or incorrect. It should be typed as Record<K, T[]>.

steps.title: Implement the array iteration logic
steps.instruction: Inside the groupBy function, add a forEach loop to iterate through each item in the input array. The array parameter should be called 'items'.
steps.hint: Use the array parameter and call .forEach() on it. The callback should receive each item as a parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The groupBy function will have a forEach loop that iterates through the input array, though it won't yet group items.
successCriteria: The groupBy function contains a forEach loop that iterates through an 'items' array parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using forEach to iterate through the items array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The iteration logic is missing. Add a forEach loop to process each item in the input array.

steps.title: Extract the key for each item using the keySelector
steps.instruction: Inside the forEach loop, call the keySelector function with the current item to get the grouping key. Store the result in a variable named 'key'.
steps.hint: Remember that keySelector is a function parameter that takes an item of type T and returns a key of type K. Use it like: const key = keySelector(item);
steps.expectedOutcome: The keySelector function is called for each item in the loop, producing a key value that will be used for grouping.
successCriteria: A variable named 'key' is declared inside the forEach loop, and its value is obtained by calling keySelector(item).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling keySelector with the current item and storing the result in a variable named 'key'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The key extraction step is missing. Inside the forEach loop, you need to call keySelector(item) to get the grouping key for each item.

steps.title: Check if the key exists in the result object
steps.instruction: Inside the forEach loop, add a conditional check to see if the current key already exists in the result object.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check whether result[key] is defined. This will determine if we need to initialize a new array or push to an existing one.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now include a conditional check for whether each key already exists in the result object before proceeding to group items.
successCriteria: An if statement is added inside the forEach loop to check if result[key] is undefined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the conditional check is placed inside the forEach loop and uses the correct key variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional check is missing or incorrectly placed. Remember to check if result[key] exists before proceeding.

steps.title: Initialize array for new keys
steps.instruction: Inside the groupBy function, in the forEach loop after checking if the key exists, add an if statement that creates an empty array for that key in the result object when the key doesn't exist yet.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check if result[key] is undefined, then assign an empty array to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now handle new keys by creating empty arrays for them before pushing items.
successCriteria: An if statement is added that checks if result[key] is undefined and initializes it with an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking if the key doesn't exist in the result object and then creating an empty array for that key.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on this specific step: we need to check if the key doesn't exist in the result object and create an empty array for it.

steps.title: Push the current item to the appropriate array
steps.instruction: Inside the forEach callback, push the current item to the array associated with its key in the result object.
steps.hint: After ensuring the key exists in the result object, access result[key] and use the .push() method to add the current item.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now correctly add each item to its corresponding grouped array in the result object.
successCriteria: The forEach callback includes a statement that pushes the current item to result[key].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're pushing the current item to the correct array in the result object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The item isn't being added to the grouped array. Check that you're using result[key].push(item) inside the forEach callback.

steps.title: Return the grouped result object
steps.instruction: Add a return statement at the end of the groupBy function to return the result object.
steps.hint: The function should return the result object, which has the type Record<K, T[]>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The groupBy function now returns the properly typed result object after grouping all items.
successCriteria: The function includes a return statement that returns the result object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Create test data and call the groupBy function to verify it groups items correctly and maintains proper types.
steps.hint: Define an array of objects with a property to group by, then call groupBy with a keySelector that extracts that property.
